functions.name: free_wrapper
functions.description: Frees a dynamically allocated memory block referenced by a pointer variable and (by convention for such wrappers) likely nulls the pointer afterward. Intended as a safe/free helper around free() for C code. Details of nulling behavior are inferred from the double-pointer signature; exact behavior is not documented in this header.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a pointer variable (void**) owned by the caller
*ptr should point to a dynamically allocated block compatible with the underlying deallocation method (likely free()), or be NULL
Thread-safety and idempotency are unknown; do not assume it can be called concurrently on the same pointer
Behavior when *ptr is invalid, already-freed, or not heap-allocated is undefined

functions.name: bdestroy_wrapper
functions.description: Destroys a bstring (from bstrlib) and likely clears the caller’s handle. This wrapper presumably calls bdestroy(*b) and may set *b to NULL to avoid dangling references. Behavior inferred from the name and the parameter type (bstring is a pointer typedef; passing bstring* allows the callee to clear it). Exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to a bstring handle (i.e., address of a bstring variable)
*b should be either a valid bstring obtained from bstrlib or NULL
Relies on bstrlib types; include and initialize bstrlib as required by your environment
Behavior when *b is invalid or already destroyed is undefined
